title: $f^!$ with rational coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with its condensed coefficient ring and pulled-back module-object interpretation of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, in that standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Write $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\Loc(\Dctf(T,\Lambda))$ for its full localizing closure [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The right adjoint $f^!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence] on these localizing categories satisfies
$$
f^!\bigl(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\bigr)\subseteq\Dctf(X,\Lambda).
$$
Its restriction is right adjoint to $Rf_!:\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: First verify the finiteness needed by the affine-cover argument. The schemes are separated and of finite type over $k$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine and quasi-compact, the finite-type definition gives finite affine covers of $X$ and $Y$. Their separatedness implies quasi-separatedness: the diagonal is a closed immersion, whose inverse image over an affine is the spectrum of a quotient ring and hence quasi-compact. Thus $X,Y$ are qcqs. By [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc], $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)=\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ and the two localizing closures agree for $T=X,Y$ and for all affine charts and affine spaces used below. It suffices to take $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$ and prove $f^!K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Statement (2); standing setting and the hypotheses of the affine-cover proof

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover $Y=\bigcup_\beta V_\beta$. By the finite-type definition, for each $V_\beta=\operatorname{Spec}R_\beta$ choose a finite affine cover $f^{-1}(V_\beta)=\bigcup_\alpha U_{\beta\alpha}$ with $U_{\beta\alpha}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{\beta\alpha}$ and $B_{\beta\alpha}$ a finitely generated $R_\beta$-algebra. Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_d$; evaluation gives a surjection $R_\beta[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\twoheadrightarrow B_{\beta\alpha}$. The affine description of a closed immersion therefore gives $i:U_{\beta\alpha}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_{V_\beta}$. Writing $p:\mathbf A^d_{V_\beta}\to V_\beta$ and $u:U_{\beta\alpha}\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V_\beta\hookrightarrow Y$, the equality of the structure ring maps gives $fu=vpi$. These are finitely many charts covering $X$. The integer $d$ may depend on the chart; no uniform choice is required.

source.place: Existence of charts; Stacks Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize

proof.text:
For each chosen chart, use the functor isomorphism in [det-thm-restriction-local], with exactly the $V,U,i,p,u,v$ constructed in step 2:
$$u^*f^!\simeq i^!p^!v^*:\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dbc(U,\Lambda)).$$
All maps have the domains required there and $fu=vpi$. This is the local factorization of the right adjoint; the lemma is used here for this functor isomorphism.

source.place: Displayed functor isomorphism, with a specified affine chart

proof.text: The restriction $v^*K$ is bounded constructible. Indeed restriction to an open is exact (kernels and cokernels of sheaves are local), so its cohomology is $\mathcal H^q(K)|_V$ with the same finite degree bounds. Intersecting a constructible stratification with $V$ and restricting its pro-étale covers and finite presentations gives the finite constant local models in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Thus $v^*K\in\Dbc(V,\Lambda)$. Apply [det-cor-affine-space-rational-induction] to this object: $L=p^!v^*K\simeq p^*v^*K(d)[2d]$ lies in $\Dbc(\mathbf A^d_V,\Lambda)$. This uses the preservation assertion of that node, as well as its isomorphism.

source.place: Second paragraph: restriction to V and rational affine-space purity

proof.text: For the closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_V$ and the object $L$ of step 4, [det-prop-closed-adjoint-constructible-support] gives $R\underline\Gamma_U L\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$. By [det-prop-closed-adjoint-constructible-yoneda], $i^!L\simeq R\underline\Gamma_U L$. Combining this with step 3 gives $u^*f^!K\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$ on every member of the finite affine cover of step 2. The supported-sections statement is applied over $\mathbf A^d_V$, not over $Y$, and its coefficient hypothesis is exactly $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

source.place: Second paragraph: closed-immersion preservation, via supported sections and Yoneda

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [det-thm-restriction-glue] to $M=f^!K$ and the finite cover in step 2. Explicitly, choose bounds $[a_U,b_U]$ for each $M|_U$; exact restriction shows $\mathcal H^q(M)=0$ outside $[\min_U a_U,\max_U b_U]$, because a sheaf zero on an open cover is zero. For each remaining degree choose the finite locally closed constructible partitions on the finitely many $U$ supplied by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Add $X\setminus U$ to each partition and take all finite intersections. The resulting nonempty pieces are locally closed and form a finite partition of $X$. They are constructible: the affine opens $U$ are retrocompact in the quasi-separated $X$; if $W$ is retrocompact open in $U$, then $W$ is retrocompact in $X$, since $W\cap T=W\cap(U\cap T)$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $T$ of $X$. Hence each Boolean expression defining a constructible subset of $U$ also defines a constructible subset of $X$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Every piece of the common refinement lies in at least one $U$, where the relevant cohomology sheaves have finite constant local models; restricting those models to the piece preserves their finite presentations. Thus all the cohomology sheaves of $M$ are constructible and $M\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$. If $X$ is empty the conclusion holds for the zero category without taking minima over an empty set.

source.place: Clause (1), boundedness and constructibility; Stacks Tag 09YD, lemma-quasi-compact-open-immersion-constructible-image

proof.text: By the equality of categories in step 1, step 6 proves $f^!\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\subseteq\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. To restrict the other functor as well, take the compactification $f=rj$ supplied within the standing setting by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. The standing setting gives $r$ proper and $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ open, with $Z$ separated and of finite type over $k$. Step 1 gives $X$ quasi-compact. Since $Z$ is separated, its diagonal is closed; over each affine open its inverse image is a quotient spectrum and is quasi-compact, so $Z$ is quasi-separated. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to $j$: it is quasi-compact, as required below. Since $Y$ is qcqs, [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] applies and says that $Rf_!=Rr_*j_!$ carries $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. Thus both functors admit restrictions to the indicated full subcategories.

source.place: Last paragraph: preservation by compact support; compactification-single statement

proof.text:
For $A\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and $K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, the adjunction of [sk-prop-sf-existence] gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))}(Rf_!A,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))}(A,f^!K).$$
For $T=X,Y$, the revised definition [sk-def-localizing-closure] takes the closure inside the unbounded module-object category $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, with no completeness condition. Every subcategory in its defining intersection contains $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$, so their intersection contains it too. The closure is full in this same ambient category, and $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ is full there by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Consequently its inclusion into the closure is full. Since step 7 puts both images in the smaller categories, these are precisely $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)}(Rf_!A,K)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dctf(X,\Lambda)}(A,f^!K)$. The maps on these Hom sets are the original maps; hence their bijectivity and naturality in $A,K$ are unchanged. This is the required restricted adjunction.

source.place: Last paragraph and displayed Hom bijection
